टीवी इंडस्ट्री से एक बेहद दुखद और चौंकाने वाली खबर सामने आई है! 💔

भारतीय टेलीविज़न के सबसे लोकप्रिय क्राइम शो CID और हॉरर शो Aahat के निर्माता बीपी सिंह का दिल का दौरा पड़ने से निधन हो गया है। 27 October की सुबह तड़के हार्ट अटैक के कारण उन्होंने अंतिम सांस ली। 

इस दुखद खबर की जानकारी फिल्म निर्माता Ashoke Pandit ने अपने सोशल मीडिया अकाउंट पर शेयर की। उन्होंने बताया कि बीपी सिंह का अंतिम संस्कार 28 October को किया जाएगा। 

Ashoke Pandit ने उन्हें श्रद्धांजलि देते हुए एक बेहतरीन फिल्ममेकर बताया। उन्होंने कहा कि बीपी सिंह के क्राइम और हॉरर शोज़ ने देश भर के दर्शकों को हमेशा बांधकर रखा। 

बता दें कि बीपी सिंह IFTDA यानी Indian Film and Television Directors' Association के प्रेसिडेंट भी रह चुके हैं। उनके जाने से एंटरटेनमेंट इंडस्ट्री में गहरा शोक है। 🎥

क्या आपने भी बचपन में CID या Aahat शो देखा है? कमेंट्स में अपनी पसंदीदा यादें शेयर करें! 👇

ctx.text:
Filmmaker and television producer BP Singh, best known for producing the popular crime shows CID and Aahat, has passed away following a heart attack. Filmmaker Ashoke Pandit shared the news on social media on Tuesday, October 27, and paid tribute to Singh, remembering him for his contribution to Indian television and their association through the Indian Film and Television Directors’ Association (IFTDA).
In his Instagram post, Pandit expressed grief over Singh’s demise and described him as a talented filmmaker whose work influenced generations of television professionals. “Sad to know about the demise of an ace Producer Director B.P.Singh ji due to massive heart attack today early morning,” Pandit wrote.
He further remembered Singh for creating crime and horror shows that became familiar names among Indian television audiences. “A brilliant filmmaker who captivated the nation with his crime shows C.I.D and AAhat. His work is still & will continue to be a an inspiration to generations to come,” he added.
Pandit also spoke about his personal association with Singh, recalling their time working together when Singh served as president of the Indian Film and Television Directors’ Association. “Was fortunate to be a very close associate of him when he was the President of @iftda_. A great human being & a dear friend,” Pandit wrote.
He added that Singh would be remembered for his contributions to the entertainment industry and offered condolences to his family and loved ones. “Will always be remembered with his contribution in the entertainment world. Heartfelt condolences to the family & near ones,” the filmmaker said.
Singh was widely known for producing CID, one of Indian television’s longest-running crime series, and Aahat, a horror anthology that became popular with viewers. Through these shows, he helped establish crime and suspense as enduring genres on Indian television.
According to Pandit’s post, Singh’s last rites are scheduled to take place on October 28, with further details to be shared later.
